text:
这轮大科技财报全部谢幕了，各家公布的 2026 全年预期 Capex 和我之前想的差不多，要么继续提高，要么保持不变，没有一家公司主动削减。

Google Capex 从 1800-1900 亿美元，上调到了 1950-2050 亿美元。

Amazon Capex 从 2000 亿美元，上调到了 2200 亿美元。

Meta Capex 提高了下限，从 1250-1450 亿美元，上调到了 1300-1450 亿美元。

微软虽然表面从 1950 亿下调到了 1750 亿，但实际上是因为会计上的一些手脚，Capex 并没有任何变化。

而且这几家大科技在财报会议上都提到了一点，目前 AI 需求远远大于供给，订单能见度非常强，算力仍然是瓶颈。

对于收支票的半导体上下游来说，未来几年订单的确定性非常高。

我想只要这些大科技能够快速完成 AI 算力变现，未来的变现速度能追得上砸钱的速度，短时间内 AI 基建投资就不会见顶，AI 主线还会继续。

The continued promotion of these claims, despite them having been clearly proven false, is an attempt to mislead the public and create a negative perception aimed at discrediting our club's transfer activities.

It is also noteworthy that the individuals and platforms responsible for these speculations were behind similar false claims during the previous season.

Galatasaray Sports Club conducts its transfer operations with the utmost care, professionalism, and confidentiality, always in the best interests of the club. False reports and speculative claims will not alter our club's principles, objectives, or approach to transfer business.

We respectfully urge the public and the great Galatasaray supporters to rely solely on official statements issued by our club and not to give credence to false reports, speculative claims, or the individuals and platforms that continue to spread them'

text:
我对 workbuddy 的一个偏见，不一定对：

workbuddy 是真好用，但不是给在座的任何一个大佬用的。

一个东西好用，有时是因为真好用，有时是因为没得选。workbuddy 是后一种。

十八年前，百度干谷歌是这样，今天的 workbuddy 也是这样。 

一年前，我听人说要人才高地学习，人才洼地赚钱。我就跟人合作，跑去做什么场景化智能体定制和 AI 培训，只做国内，嗯，差不多就是做外包，现在的说法叫 FDE。

那时候我第一次认真学习怎么用百度搜索才能搜索出想要的，第一次学会用 gitee，第一次知道有些企业工作环境全内网不是传说。也第一次知道全民都在讨论 AI 落地，满口都是 chatgpt、 deepseek r1 满血版，但是真正能用得起都是 qwen 蒸馏版。也是第一次知道为什么 qwen 会火，高端的局它上不了，但低端的 qwen3.5-27b，那是是千万小企业最好的也是唯一的药。

后来也经常给别人装装龙虾 和 cc。今天龙虾装完了，明天 cc 被封了。今天cc 正常了，明天龙虾连不了外网了。又过几天，安装 codex 的 windows 用户问我 home 是什么盘，codex 说它删了它，可是它电脑上只有 cd 盘啊。再来他的 codex 就挂了，他要找我全款退款，不然就举报我。

最难忘的一次是，有天我们去给一家几十人的传统企业搞 AI 培训。完了领导说你们今天讲的不错，钱的事情，等我 xx 项目回款了就背靠背开票打款给你。哦对了，你们今天用的那个「必应」是什么，感觉比百度厉害啊，能不能改天找人来给我们全员培训下。
我和朋友笑笑无奈的说好。

那时候的日子，我一天也不想过，就跟朋友分手，自己跑出来干独立开发。

上个月，朋友跟我说现在他活过来了，累死累活跟我干了一年，现在回款五分之一都没收到，而现在有了 workbuddy，一切都简单了。

workbuddy 就是国内中小企业培训最好的教具，甚至没有备选项。认知这方面腾讯满大街的广告为你抹平了，体验也跟豆包差不多，上手难度 0。

作为培训讲师你一提 workbuddy 大家甚至都会抢答了，那个办公版的豆包嘛。 

自然很多售前、售中、售后麻烦就少很多，甚至有问题大家也找你直接找腾讯，腾讯的产品么。当然带来的后果也显而易见，报价只能更低了，大众的东西就这样，一旦被人熟知的，就没信息差了。但朋友确开心了，毕竟蚊子腿再小也是肉，以前干那些 FDE 外包，报价是高，但回不了款就特么只是浮盈啊，毛用没有。

上周我问朋友我能不能现在学习 workbuddy，然后继续干老本行。朋友说，可能来不及了，现在外面全是同行啊，抖音上，小红书上，B 站上，你看得见的地方都是同行。

我说，完了，这场办公 AI 竞赛结束了，workbuddy 营销推广已经形成闭环了，现在停掉广告估计都能自我运转。workbuddy 唯一需要注意的就是跟它爸爸说，自家兄弟产品注意啊，将所有给 codex work，claude cowork 产品的流量换成 workbuddy。

豆包啊，千问啊，想转型估计太晚了。但也不好说，万一哪天 workbuddy 不像豆包一样免费送 token 鸡蛋了，说不定人们又会去追溯新潮流。

坦白说，像豆包一样，workbuddy 也算为民谋福利了，十几年后再来看，在 AI 科普提升全面认知这事上也是功劳一件了。

毕竟一个东西好用，有时是因为没得选。有时候没得选是因为真的没得选，有时候没得选是认知上不允许选。

毕竟国内 99.9% 的人不像推特上的大佬，有钱的 claude code 、codex 全都要，没钱的闲鱼买买日抛也凑合，再不济嫖嫖各个海外产品免费版也不是不能用么。

这样你所有的能量都能用来做这件事。
一不小心你就克服了拖延症，变得更强大了。

text:
过去三年美股涨了多少你知道，但你账户的实际收益是多少你敢看吗？

标普500三年涨了将近100%。纳指涨得更多。如果你2023年买了一只SPY什么都不做，到今天翻了一倍。

但大部分散户的实际收益远远跑不赢指数。有数据的，摩根大通统计过，年交易超过200次的散户平均年化收益是负的。负的。指数在翻倍，你在亏钱。

为什么？因为你在每一次暴跌中割肉，在每一次反弹中追高。昨天道指跌1100点你割了。今天涨2.8%你犹豫了不敢追。等涨到5%你追了。下周再跌你又割了。

你全年交易了200次，每次赚一点亏一点，但手续费和滑点在每一次交易中都稳稳地扣着你。200次交易的手续费加起来，可能吃掉了你全年的收益。

而你妈如果2023年不知道听了谁的话买了一只SPY然后忘了密码，到今天翻了一倍。

你研究了三年K线，看了一千篇分析报告，熬了几百个夜盯盘，关注了三十个博主，加了十个交流群。你的收益不如你妈忘了密码。

这不是段子，这是统计学事实。

最赚钱的策略是最无聊的策略。这句话你听了一百遍了。你永远在听，永远在点头，然后永远在下一次暴跌的时候按下卖出按钮。

你的对手不是市场，不是机构，不是美联储，是你自己那只管不住的手。

Uli Hoeneß says he's very happy with Bayern's summer transfer window:

"We've had a perfect transfer window, just like last year, bringing in two players who will be very useful to us.

Regarding players we sold, the individual fees may have been relatively small, but in the end they still added up to a very respectable amount. We recently had a meeting with Herbert Hainer and several members of our supervisory board, and he [Eberl] reported that we've already generated more than €40 million in income.

If we can now manage to move one or two more players on, which is what we'd like to do, that would be ideal. But I also want to make one thing absolutely clear: a contract with FC Bayern is sacrosanct. In other words, if we ultimately can't find a solution, then we have to keep those players."

text:
7月这波行情确实太难了，不只是追高的韭菜被埋，连专业基金都已经跪了好几个。

天才少年 Leopold 并不孤单；据彭博报道，明汯关联的海外基金 Jupiter Tactical Trading Fund。它年初管理规模约 1.86 亿美元，上半年费后收益还超过 90%，结果 7 月前三天只亏不到 7.5%，到 7 月 24 日，亏损已经迅速扩大到约 43%。

最扎眼的是，这还是一只“市场中性”量化基金。

理论上，它不应该太依赖大盘涨跌；但当 AI、小盘股和动量因子同时反转，市场中性也救不了：多头快速崩，空头突然逼空，原本稳定的相关性和对冲关系一起失效，再叠加杠杆和赎回压力，净值几周内就能被打穿。

这轮行情反转速度太快，拥挤交易一起踩踏，连有些最聪明的钱都来不及撤。

7 月，已经变成专业基金大型压力测试现场。

text:
简单说下，为什么我没有用现在 subagent/临时 worker 模式；核心是我认为 agent 想要工作好，就是要花时间盯着轨迹，通过 prompt/装工具来调教它。
codex/manus 这些 agent runtime/harness 会在他们的目标领域，调研，Web 开发，code，提前调教好。
但每个人的工作都有自己的特殊性，如果超脱这个范围就会出现，agent 瞎干活，质量下降，或者成本爆炸。
所以临时 worker 这种 一个 prompt，one-shot 中间不做干预（也没有历史 trajectory 去 follow） 只适合非常小非常具体，边界 spec 摸的非常熟的任务。

text:
Citadel is not the bad guy in this story. 

When you are investing billions and make 20x returns in 2 years, you attract the notice of all the hedge funds. It was obvious to everyone that Leopold had to be using excessive leverage to get those returns.

Taking out a player who doesn't have enough liquidity to cover leverage and manage a downturn is so common on Wall Street, it's one of their basic tools to enhance their own returns. 

No, the person who should be blamed for Leopold's implosion is Leopold himself. 

Hedge funds do use *some* leverage themselves, but boy do they analyze the snot out of those positions to ensure what happened to Leopold doesn't happen to them. Leopold either didn't do that basic analysis or got it comically wrong.

Players like Citadel actually *help* the market by taking out the yahoos who end up causing excessive market volatility through leverage. If you know you could get pounced on by the likes of Citadel, then you won't put yourself in a position to be pounced on and thus won't cause undue market volatility.

quotedTweet.text:
OH. MY. GOODNESS. 

CITADEL HAS BOUGHT A MAJORITY OF THE PUBLIC ASSETS FROM LEOPOLD'S SITUATIONAL AWARENESS FUND.

So...Citadel scares everyone on Tuesday about a surprise rate hike during FOMC that WE ALL KNEW was not going to happen...

On Wednesday, the entire market freaks out about the rate hike which causes the selling to compound on itself creating 50-70% drawdowns across the board in high beta semicondcutor names...

Which means Leopold who we now know had $45B of assets and was 400% LEVERED ends up being the sacrifice as he gets liquidated at what theoretically could be the bottom due to not having the margin requirements to keep solvent...

AND THE PERSON WHO CAUSED THE SELLOFF WITH THE RATE HIKE FEARS ENDS UP COMING IN TO BUY HIS ASSETS FOR 40 TO 50 CENTS ON THE DOLLAR. 

By the way, Leopold is getting married this weekend. I think he wanted to make sure he wasn't getting margin called during his wedding.

A vet on wall street in Ken Griffin takes out the young new kid. 

ABSOLUTE. CINEMA.

text:
无人机里那颗芯片是 ARM，但不跑 Linux。

很多人觉得算力越强越能解决问题——树莓派 2.4GHz 四核，STM32 几百 MHz 单核，凭什么无人机里用 STM32？

答案藏在电机控制的物理本质里。无刷电机的换相循环每 40-62 微秒必须完成一整轮：读转子位置、算该给哪几相线圈通电、更新 PWM。错过一轮，转子已经转过去了，你还在用旧位置算出来的电压——换相时刻就错了，电流尖峰、力矩抖动，严重就烧管。

电机控制要的不是"平均很快"，是"最坏情况也不慢"。

树莓派跑 Linux，GPIO 中断延迟最快 9-11μs，但会跳——USB 收发、内核调度、X server 任何一个打断都能让某次延迟飘到几十上百μs。Linux 的实时线程本质是"尽力而为"，内核调度这层永远在。

STM32 的 Cortex-M 裸机中断延迟几十到几百纳秒，抖动极小，测一万次方差几乎可忽略。NVIC 是硬件级抢占，没有"内核调度"中间层。定时器自动触发 ADC，ADC 自动喂 DMA，CPU 全程不参与——硬件流水线，不是软件驱动。

ARM 有两条线：Cortex-A 跑 Linux 追求吞吐，Cortex-M 不跑 Linux 追求确定性。STM32 高端 H7 480MHz、N6 800MHz，算力直逼应用处理器，但仍然不跑 Linux。这个"够强但不带 Linux 包袱"的位置，就是工业实时控制的甜区。

一个是尽量快，一个是永远不慢——在电机这个物理世界里，这两件事的差距就是能不能好好转的差距。

https://t.co/CLbe8TCxiL

text:
别死刷 LeetCode 了，OpenAI 刚流出的 2026 工程师面经，直接给我看楞了：人家已经开始考你怎么和 AI 搭档写代码了，你还在刷五年前的算法脑筋急转弯。

这是 Reddit 刚爆的新鲜热乎面经，候选人刚走完整个流程，和谷歌 Meta 那种纯考 DSA 八股的路子完全不一样，6 轮面下来，根本不给刷题家留一点活路。

给你们拆得明明白白：
1️⃣初筛根本不走流程
别以为 HR 面就是问你期望薪资、为什么来 OpenAI，人家上来先聊 “你觉得 AI 未来会往哪走”—— 说白了根本不缺能写代码的人，先筛认知和价值观同频的，连 OpenAI 自己的 Charter 都没读过的，直接就刷了。

2️⃣技术初筛全是生产场景
同一天连考俩，各一小时：手写带版本控制的键值存储，设计带容错的任务调度器。没有接雨水、爬楼梯这种脱离实际的脑筋急转弯，全是工程师上班天天要碰的真问题。

3️⃣回家作业根本混不过去
48 小时时间，让你做一个带重试机制、死信队列的分布式 Webhook 投递系统，不是几十行的玩具 demo，是真能上线跑的生产级项目。别想着抄个开源项目交差，后面有狠的等着。

4️⃣逐行代码拷问才是真杀招
面试官拿着你交的作业逐行走查，你每选一个方案、每写一个判断，他都要追着问为什么这么做，为什么不选别的方案，权衡点在哪。抄来的代码你根本讲不出背后的逻辑，一开口就露馅。

5️⃣Onsite 四轮全是硬货
▫️ 第一轮 coding 是渐进式关卡制，必须把当前阶段跑通才能进下一关，比如先实现 token 级流式 diff，再做状态追踪，再做回滚，背的模板根本套不上，一步卡壳就没了；
▫️ 第二轮 coding 往深了考系统能力，并发控制、内存效率、Python 生成器 / 异步这些写业务天天踩坑的点，全是实操出来的经验，背书背不出来；
▫️ 系统设计直接让你画 ChatGPT 的架构，考 GPU 怎么调度、流量突增怎么自动扩缩容、分布式节点怎么协调，全是他们自己天天在解决的真问题，没什么假大空的通用模板；
▫️ 行为面别背 “我遇到困难迎难而上” 的套话，要听你真的主导过的跨团队架构决策，当时有什么选项，你选了什么，付出了什么代价，拿到了什么结果，全要具体的 tradeoff，空话直接过。

6️⃣最反常识的 Beta 加试
现在部分候选人会遇到额外一轮：给你一个现有代码库，放一个人根本不可能短时间写完的大需求，让你用 AI 编码 Agent 协作完成。人家根本不防着你用 AI，反而直接把 “和 AI 搭档干活的能力” 摆上了考场，这才是真的在招 2026 年的工程师，不是招十年前的码农。

我看完最大的感受是，传统大厂那套选人逻辑真的过时了：
▫️ 纯刷题的时代彻底翻篇，LeetCode 刷得再熟，做不了真实系统、讲不清决策逻辑，根本过不了关；

▫️ 代码跑通只是最低要求，能想明白每一个选择的代价和收益，才是工程师和搬砖的区别；

▫️ 会用 AI 早就不是什么加分项，很快就是工程师的标配能力，你还在抵触 AI 抢工作，人家已经把和 AI 协作当面试必考点了。

给准备冲的人提几个实在醒：

别抱着题本死磕了，多写点真实的分布式小项目，把语言底层的并发、内存逻辑摸透，准备几个你真刀真枪做过的、有取舍的架构故事，

现在就开始练怎么给 AI 派活、审 AI 的代码、和 AI 一起搭系统。等这套面试逻辑全行业铺开的时候，你连该刷什么题都不知道。

你们觉得这种考真实能力的面试，和传统刷 LeetCode 比，哪个更难？

#OpenAI #程序员面试 #AI编程 #工程师求职

On the $20 Plus plan, the usage allowance for GPT-5.6 Luna is almost the same as the allowance for GPT-5.6 Sol on the $200 Pro plan.

I think it is a great strategy to offer a model that is roughly one generation behind at the lowest-priced subscription tier with such generous usage limits.

Until now, users on the $20 plan could barely try the advanced models, so I did not feel comfortable recommending it to people around me. But now, I think it is finally good enough to recommend.

I hope OpenAI continues with this strategy going forward.

🇺🇸 English

THE LIGHTHOUSE LOOK | AXTI / TONGMEI

Bottom Line

AXTI remains one of the few publicly traded ways to gain exposure to Beijing Tongmei’s indium phosphide platform. Investor focus continues to center on AI optical networking, Tongmei’s strategic Hong Kong listing transition, expanding InP production capacity, and execution following recent commercial supply agreements. The investment thesis remains driven by long term AI infrastructure demand rather than short term market volatility.

⸻

🇨🇳 简体中文（Simplified）

灯塔观察 | AXTI / 通美晶体

核心观点

AXTI 仍然是全球资本市场中少数能够投资北京通美磷化铟业务的平台之一。市场关注重点仍然集中于人工智能光通信需求、通美香港上市规划、磷化铟产能扩张以及近期商业合作的持续执行。长期投资逻辑依然建立在全球 AI 基础设施的发展，而非短期股价波动。

⸻

🇯🇵 日本語（Japanese）

ライトハウス・ルック | AXTI / Tongmei

要点

AXTI は、北京 Tongmei のインジウムリン事業へ投資できる数少ない上場企業の一つです。市場は AI 光通信需要、香港上場戦略、InP 生産能力拡大、そして商業契約の進展に注目しています。長期的な投資テーマは、短期的な株価変動ではなく、世界的な AI インフラ拡大にあります。

⸻

🇰🇷 한국어（Korean）

라이트하우스 룩 | AXTI / Tongmei

핵심 내용

AXTI는 베이징 Tongmei의 인듐인화물(InP) 사업에 투자할 수 있는 대표적인 상장 기업입니다. 시장은 AI 광통신 수요 확대, Tongmei의 홍콩 상장 전략, InP 생산 능력 확대 및 최근 공급 계약의 이행을 주목하고 있습니다. 장기 투자 논리는 단기 주가 변동보다 AI 인프라 성장에 기반하고 있습니다.

⸻

🇸🇦 العربية (Arabic)

نظرة المنارة | AXTI / Tongmei

الخلاصة

تظل شركة AXTI إحدى الشركات المدرجة القليلة التي توفر للمستثمرين تعرضًا مباشرًا لأعمال Tongmei في مجال فوسفيد الإنديوم. ويتركز اهتمام السوق على البنية التحتية للذكاء الاصطناعي، وتقنيات الشبكات الضوئية، وخطة إدراج Tongmei في هونغ كونغ، وتوسيع الطاقة الإنتاجية، وتنفيذ اتفاقيات التوريد الأخيرة. وتستند أطروحة الاستثمار طويلة الأجل إلى نمو الذكاء الاصطناعي العالمي أكثر من تقلبات السوق قصيرة الأجل.

text:
The first era of Cyber AI shifted advantage to the attacker. The next is about taking back control. 
 
AI-powered attacks now move at machine speed. Even if defenders use AI, attackers still choose the time, place, and first move. In a head-to-head race, the attacker has the edge. 
 
Defenders need to change the equation. Not by running faster, but by turning attacker automation into a liability.  
 
Every autonomous attack depends on an AI agent's ability to interpret its environment and determine the next step in the cyber kill chain. That dependency creates a new point of leverage. With the right defenses, organizations can exploit that weakness to disrupt attacker decision-making and buy more time to detect, contain, and respond. 
 
That's Counter AI, and we've built the tech to shift advantage back to defenders.  
 
Register to learn where cyber defense goes next from Booz Allen Cyber Leaders Brad Medairy, Andrew Turner, and Aaron Sant-Miller: https://t.co/NA7A2eGajH

text:
🚨 New Episode: The Legacy of Congressman Tim Murphy: The Late Psychologist, Navy Reserve Officer, Author, & Mental Health Reformer Shares Wisdom on Navigating Congress, Trauma, & Faith in a Life of Public Service

Political Trade Secrets: Join me and my guest Dr. Tim Murphy—licensed psychologist, former Pennsylvania Congressman, former Pennsylvania State Senator, former commander in the U.S. Navy Reserve, mental health reform leader, and author of The Christ Cure, The Angry Child, and Overcoming Passive Aggression—as we pull back the curtain on Congress, public service, mental health reform, trauma, faith, and what it really takes to help people through politics.

Recorded shortly before Dr. Murphy’s unexpected passing, this conversation now serves as a meaningful reflection on the causes and convictions that shaped his life’s work: healing families in crisis, supporting veterans and first responders, reforming the way America treats serious mental illness, and reminding leaders that public service should be about more than ego, status, or political theater.

The episode explores:

• What Dr. Murphy learned as a psychologist about power, leadership, narcissism, and the psychological toll of public life in Washington
• Why he believed people should not run for office just to say something, but because they have something important to say
• How Congress really works behind the scenes, from legislative “sausage-making” to the hard reality of passing major reforms without receiving the credit
• The story behind Dr. Murphy’s landmark mental health reform work, including the bill that passed the House 422–2 before becoming part of the 21st Century Cures Act
• Why he believed America must distinguish between broad “mental health” and serious mental illness, especially when dealing with schizophrenia, homelessness, addiction, and families in crisis
• How serving in the Navy Reserve and working with traumatic brain injury and PTSD patients at Walter Reed reshaped how he viewed politics and service
• Why faith, forgiveness, humility, purpose, and community are central to healing trauma, especially for veterans, first responders, and those who love them
• How Dr. Murphy’s books, articles, and work through Gunny’s Ridge continue his mission of helping the broken, the hurting, and those carrying unseen wounds

text:
New TEQ episode with @ecoangelhsu, founder of the Data-Driven EnviroLab at UNC Chapel Hill and co-developer of ChatNetZero, the first chatbot built to scrutinize net zero pledges.

We recorded this after sharing a panel at London Climate Week, and it went straight at the questions most sustainability conversations skip. Why measuring badly is worse than not measuring at all. Why 96% of large companies disclosing to CDP still fail on at least one core metric. Why generic LLMs will tell you that you can pledge net zero and keep burning fossil fuels. And whether climate AI can justify its own energy use.

Angel has spent 20 years in this space, starting on the Greenhouse Gas Protocol, and she talks about the parts nobody reports: the failures, the setbacks, the good, the bad, and the ugly. Her closing point on why we need to normalize failure in climate reporting is the one I keep coming back to.

quotedTweet.text:
For 18 months we've been chasing one idea: 

What if hiring gave you the best of both worlds instead of forcing a choice?

Because right now, a choice is all you get.

Job boards are cheap. That's the whole pitch. They're slow, frustrating, and the quality people are nearly impossible to identify in the pile. You get what you pay for.

Recruiters are better, in some ways. Vetted talent, curated to your needs. But they're slow, they're expensive, and they're not you, so the match is never quite right. An arm and a leg for something you could do yourself, if anyone gave you the tools.

Both have their place. But, both are full of friction.

The best of both worlds means the power of a recruiter with the choice of a job board, and technology stripping the friction out of every step between them.

That's what we built. Scout OS: a searchable marketplace of pre-vetted global talent. 

Search a role, get matches, watch 2-minute intro videos, shortlist who fits, schedule interviews, hire, onboard. 

Browse free. Pay only when you hire.

It goes public in August. Before that, we're launching the Founding 100.

100 SMB and mid-market companies who help us take Scout OS from good to great. Not spectators. Members use the platform for real, at least one hire in the first 90 days, so we get honest usage while it matters most. 

After each hire, a short feedback form and a 10-minute call: what's missing, what you'd change, what you'd remove. We want the criticism most of all, though we won't turn down a compliment. And when new features land, the 100 see them before the public does, and their take decides what ships.

In return, the best offer we know how to make. 
-Half off every hire, forever. 
-No platform fee, ever. 
-Double referral fees for everyone you send our way. 

And a private Slack with the other 99 companies and our team, where what you say steers what we build next.

Almost 40 seats are already filled and we haven’t even announced it, until now. Applying takes one email, and we personally call every company we pick.

https://t.co/ZHRNXaZVNy

text:
Today SMG (Shepherd Model Gateway), an engine-agnostic gateway for LLM inference, has officially graduated from LightSeek Foundation and moves to a new independent home:
https://t.co/YC7QfM0YUR
SMG was the first project incubated by the LightSeek Foundation and was recently accepted into the @PyTorch Ecosystem. It has now reached the point where its next stage should be driven by the broader open-source community.
Why now?
Over the past few months — supporting Day 0 launches for leading open models and maintaining inference engines day to day — it became clear how much of the frontend and gateway layer is genuinely shared across engines. Some of those shared components are already running in production today, and maintainers from TokenSpeed and @vllm_project will keep building them with SMG. Rather than every project maintaining these pieces independently, they're better built once, together.
Model provider protocols have also kept evolving beyond the traditional OpenAI-compatible API, which makes this a good moment to revisit SMG's architecture for the next generation of model interfaces.
Fundamentally this move is about governance. SMG is built by contributors across several companies and inference projects, and it should stay that way: community-driven, maintained across the ecosystem, owned by a broader open-source community. Shared infrastructure makes everyone stronger.
Whether you maintain an inference engine, serve models at scale, or care about where AI serving infrastructure goes next, there's room for you here.

text:
How Do You Grade AI Work That Has No Right Answer?

Imagine that you’re a business leader about to sign a deal for an AI tool that drafts business cases. Ask it a specific question: “Should we enter this market?” and it evaluates the problem within the context of your company's situation and comes back with a structured recommendation: the case for, the case against, the risk involved and a final call.

The memo is well written, in a way that would make any business school graduate proud. Which is great, but here’s the problem: how do you know that it’s a good recommendation? Unlike a university class, there is no answer key. You could of course try out the tool; but even if the output seems on track, how do you know that it will work equally well over time? Under different conditions?

Right now, most companies answer that question the only way they can: on faith. They like the demo, they trust the vendor, so they pull the trigger and deploy, hoping for the best.

This is not a flaw in the tool. The problem is that AI now produces a new kind of work that's open-ended, with no single right answer and no unit test that goes red or green. The natural instinct is to shrug and call it subjective. That’s tempting, but incomplete: "no right answer" does not mean "no standard for quality”, it means that the standard isn't sitting in an answer key waiting to be looked up.

Before you can tell whether open-ended AI work is good - not just well-written - you have to make "good" explicit: define a repeatable rubric a machine can apply at scale.

Capture The Judgment, Don't Invent It
So you can't just “take a look”. Eyeballing doesn't scale, for two reasons:
  - Every output is fluent and well-written, so flaws get hidden.
  - Every output is different: unlike ordinary software, a language model can return a different answer every time you ask, even with identical inputs.

How do we handle this in our daily work life? An experienced person already has a standard; they know that a market-entry case needs sound reasoning, a fair hearing of the downside, and evidence where evidence is possible. That judgment is usually tacit, living in one person's head.

So the move for evaluating the AI output is to capture that judgment. Write it down as a rubric: a set of named axes, each defining what strong versus weak looks like. Then the AI applies it at scale, consistently, the same way every time. It doesn't invent what "good" means for each iteration; you do, only once.

One Standard, Three Jobs
That one rubric then pays off in three ways. It tells you whether today's memo is good enough to act on (accept), whether a change to the prompt or model quietly dropped quality (regression), and where the work is weakest, so you know what to fix next (improvement). And that last job is the real payoff: it isn’t just an acceptance gate, it’s how you make the tool itself better over time.

None of this needs an answer key. Instead, make "good" explicit and capture it as a repeatable rubric - one standard doing three jobs. It's the same move as reading your codebase once and projecting many documents from it, described in my last post; do the expensive thinking once, then reuse it many ways.

This is one part of the solution. What we’ve bought with this approach is a consistent standard - the same work judged the same way every time; but by itself that’s not sufficient. It is not the same as being right. The rubric is a proxy, and the AI applying it is itself a fallible judge that can be confidently wrong.

So who checks the checker? That's the subject of the next post.

产品往往被模型和 Agent 吞噬掉，至于服务都是苦活累活，而且要处理的事情大部分都是非 AI 的传统企业需求。

最后你会发现，AI 能力像以前学外语专业的，没它肯定不行，但这是一种附加能力，它不是你的核心竞争力。

text:
You don't need to learn Linux anymore. You just talk to it.

I turned a NieR:Automata Hyprland rice into a complete operating shell. 

Underneath it's Arch. Every terminal, every config file, the complete Linux experience when you want your hands on the machine.

On top of it lives SAGE, an AI secretary built into the compositor itself: if you're not technical, you tell it what you want in plain English and it happens. Open apps, manage files, check your calendar, send a text. My grandmother could run Arch. I still get to be the guy who runs Arch.

Everything in this video is part of the shell,  nothing is a web app:

 • SAGE. An AI secretary with real control of the machine, local model, sees the screen
 • Full file manager with GPG encryption built in
 • Privacy stack. Tor, WireGuard, kill switch, DNS shield, one panel
 • Live satellite + aircraft tactical display(not shown in publicly. . . yet)
 • Discord voice calls from the desktop, no client window
 • Music player wired to my actual YT Music library
 • A polkit agent I wrote because the stock ones kept dying
 • A lockscreen that's a working clickwrap contract. Terms of Access displayed, affirmative assent required, timestamped log. It defines who's authorized on this machine, on the record
 • Light/dark theme that re-skins the terminal in real time

~14,000 lines of my own QML and Python in 96 days.
